# Voters Support Freedom and Democracy in Major Night for Civil Rights and Liberties


November 4, 2026 12:30 am


---


Spokesperson


[Deirdre Schifeling › ACLU she/her](https://www.aclu.org/bios/deirdre-schifeling)


Media Contact


media@aclu.org(212) 549-2666


125 Broad Street


18th Floor


New York, NY 10004


United States


WASHINGTON – Following race projection announcements in key campaigns and in races that will determine the control of Congress, the American Civil Liberties Union released the following statement from **Chief Political and Advocacy Officer Deirdre Schifeling** on the results so far of the 2026 midterm elections:


“Tonight, voters sent a clear message to politicians: You work for us. Since the day President Trump took office, his administration and allies have been working overtime to take away voters’ power. But American voters have shown through historic turnout that they’ve had enough of a rigged system designed to work for the people in power instead of for them.


“From key state supreme court races in Michigan and North Carolina to state legislative races in Georgia and North Carolina, voters uniformly rejected candidates who threaten abortion rights and our right to vote. Voters also stood up for reproductive freedom in Missouri and Virginia, and permanently secured voting rights and marriage equality in Virginia.


“However, our work is only half done, and now a new chapter begins. With a new Congress in Washington and state legislative sessions starting in January, now is our moment to create the representative, accountable democracy we have always deserved and remedy the failures of our system that led us to this point. We must unrig the system and ensure that government is used to make ordinary people’s lives better, not to enrich and entrench those in power.”


As part of the ACLU’s “Firewall for Freedom” strategy, the organization and its PAC, ACLU Voter Education Fund, made their[largest-ever commitment](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/aclu-launches-campaign-to-protect-rights-up-and-down-ballot) in down ballot races, spending $25.5 million across underfunded but critical state-level campaigns with an outsized impact on our rights and freedoms, from key ballot initiatives to state Supreme Court races, secretaries of state races, and state legislative races.

Civil Liberties


Criminal Law Reform


### Daves v. Mosley


Section 131 of the newly enacted Enhance Law Enforcement Integrity Act gives Coloradans a cause of action to seek damages or equitable relief when state or local police officers violate the Colorado Constitution. In 2022, Christopher Mosley sued Officer Brendan Daves for conducting a warrantless search of his car, which Daves argued was lawful under the federal protective sweep doctrine. After Mosley prevailed at trial and the court of appeals affirmed, Daves appealed to the Colorado Supreme Court. The ACLU’s State Supreme Court Initiative and the ACLU of Colorado filed an amicus brief agreeing with Mosley’s argument that Daves has misapprehended the federal doctrine whilst focusing on a separate point: the Court’s interpretation of Section 131 is not bound by federal law.


**Status:** Ongoing

### ACLU Celebrates the Legacy of Dolores Huerta


NEW YORK – The American Civil Liberties Union celebrates the legacy of Dolores Huerta, who passed away today at the age of 96. Huerta was one of the most influential workers’ rights leaders of the 20th century. Anthony D. Romero, ACLU executive director, had the following reaction to today’s news: “Dolores Huerta spent her life challenging injustice in every form – fighting for workers’ rights, women’s rights, immigrants’ rights, and so much more. Her bravery, perseverance, and compassion changed this country for the better. “As co-founder of the United Farm Workers Union, she successfully organized farmworker walkouts and consumer boycotts to demand better working conditions for Latino farmworkers. Today, millions of workers enjoy the protections that Ms. Huerta, and thousands of others who marched and mobilized alongside her, fought so hard to win. “The ACLU was proud to honor Ms. Huerta with the ACLU’s Roger N. Baldwin Medal of Liberty in 1993, recognizing her lifetime contributions to civil rights and civil liberties. More than three decades later, her continued legacy of standing up to injustice has stood the test of time. History will remember Dolores Huerta as a modern-day trailblazer for our rights and freedoms, and the ACLU will continue the fight to protect the justice and freedoms she spent her life working to achieve.”


[Aclu Celebrates The Legacy Of Dolores Huerta. Explore Press Release.](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/aclu-celebrates-the-legacy-of-dolores-huerta)

Michigan Supreme Court


Oct 2026


Civil Liberties


Criminal Law Reform


### People v. Taylor


In 2013, Michigan passed the Michigan Indigent Defense Commission Act (MIDCA) to ensure that indigent criminal defendants—that is, those who cannot afford to pay for counsel themselves—received constitutionally adequate counsel, paid for by the state. This case concerns whether and under what circumstances trial courts can, consistent with MIDCA, order indigent criminal defendants to pay the state back for their attorneys. The ACLU’s State Supreme Court Initiative, the ACLU of Michigan, and the Michigan State Planning Body filed an amicus brief in the Michigan Supreme Court arguing that MIDCA, properly construed, partially abrogated a different statute authorizing trial courts to assess attorney fees against indigent defendants and explaining that allowing such orders would undermine Michiganders’ right to counsel.


**Status:** Ongoing

### ACLU Voter Education Fund and ACLU of Georgia Launch $250K Campaign to Educate Georgia Voters Ahead of Midterms


ATLANTA – The ACLU of Georgia and the ACLU Voter Education Fund are spending $250,000 in select Georgia House races to inform voters that their civil rights and liberties, including voting rights and abortion, are on the ballot this November. The ACLU Voter Education Fund will send over 225,000 mail pieces to educate voters about candidates in State House Districts 48, 53, and 105. These state races include communities like Lawrenceville, Peachtree Corners, and Sandy Springs and are highly contested. The ACLU Voter Education Fund is investing in these races because the elected candidates will influence civil rights and liberties statewide for at least two years. Their decisions will affect voting rights, reproductive rights, privacy, and other fundamental liberties. On the voter guides, residents will see candidates’ responses to questions about those issues, such as whether they would vote to repeal Georgia’s six-week abortion ban or whether they will work to prevent unnecessary restrictions on early and absentee voting. “Georgia voters have a right to know the positions that the candidates take on the rights and freedoms that shape their lives,” said Christopher Bruce, deputy executive director, ACLU of Georgia. “We’re making sure voters get the information they need to understand the issues in these elections and what the candidates would do if they had the power of the Georgia House. From reproductive freedom and voting rights to safeguarding privacy and other liberties, the choices made under the Gold Dome can have a lasting impact on our communities.” While the ACLU Voter Education Fund does not endorse or oppose any candidates, the six-figure campaign will educate voters about the candidates’ positions on key civil rights issues, including abortion, birth control, marriage equality, and voting rights for Indigenous communities, through direct mail, radio ads, and digital ads.
